exposure: Meconium-stained amniotic fluid (MSAF) thickness (thin vs. thick)
cohort: The study involved 280 pregnancies with meconium-stained amniotic fluid at a tertiary care hospital in Kolkata.
finding: Thick meconium-stained amniotic fluid is a significant predictor of adverse neonatal outcomes, including a higher need for resuscitation, poorer Apgar scores, and increased NICU admissions.
mod_finding: Spontaneous vaginal delivery was significantly more common in cases of thin meconium compared to thick meconium.
